description: The figure is a single table rendered as an image: a four-row by six-column matrix of physiochemical property values for the constituent elements of a non-equiatomic FeMnNiAlSiC high entropy steel. The column headers, printed in bold above a horizontal rule, are the six elements Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si and C. The row labels down the left side are "Atomic radius (Å)", "Density (g/cc)", "Melting point (°C)" and "Self-diffusion coefficient (m²/s)". Printed atomic radii are Fe 1.27, Mn 1.40, Ni 1.24, Al 1.40, Si 1.11 and C 0.91 Å; densities are Fe 7.87, Mn 7.4, Ni 8.91, Al 2.70, Si 2.3 and C 2.1 g/cc; melting points are Fe 1536, Mn 1244, Ni 1455, Al 660, Si 1414 and C 3550 °C. Self-diffusion coefficients span 10⁻¹⁹ (Al) to 10⁻⁶² (Si) m²/s, with Fe 10⁻³¹, Mn 10⁻³⁶, Ni 10⁻³⁶ and the carbon entry given only as a dash. The table supplies the elemental input data — atomic-size mismatch, density and diffusivity contrasts — used to rationalise phase formation and sintering behaviour. No plot, micrograph, axis or scale bar is present.

subfigures.description: Single unlabelled table: 4 property rows (Atomic radius (Å), Density (g/cc), Melting point (°C), Self-diffusion coefficient (m²/s)) × 6 element columns (Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si, C). All numeric cells are legible; the C self-diffusion cell contains a dash.

observations.observation: The figure is a single table with 6 element columns (Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si, C) and 4 property rows, with no plot, image or scale bar.
Printed atomic radii (Å): Fe 1.27, Mn 1.40, Ni 1.24, Al 1.40, Si 1.11, C 0.91 — Mn and Al share the largest value and C the smallest.
Printed densities (g/cc): Fe 7.87, Mn 7.4, Ni 8.91, Al 2.70, Si 2.3, C 2.1 — Ni is the densest and C the least dense listed element.
Printed melting points (°C): Fe 1536, Mn 1244, Ni 1455, Al 660, Si 1414, C 3550 — Al melts lowest and C highest.
Printed self-diffusion coefficients (m²/s): Fe 10⁻³¹, Mn 10⁻³⁶, Ni 10⁻³⁶, Al 10⁻¹⁹, Si 10⁻⁶²; the value spans roughly 43 orders of magnitude across the six elements.
The self-diffusion coefficient cell for carbon contains a dash, i.e. no value is tabulated for C.
The row label is written exactly as 'Self-diffusion coefficient (m²/s)' with the unit placed on a second line inside the row label.
The caption states the table lists physiochemical properties of constituent elements in non-equiatomic FeMnNiAlSiC HES.
The paper title identifies the studied material as low-density Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high entropy steel processed by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
The caption gives no numeric values beyond those already printed in the table; no derived quantities, units conversions or source references for the property values are stated.
